B10C001.summary: After the defeat, the three surviving Kaurava warriors, Ashvatthama, Kripa and Kritavarma, flee south and then east into a dense forest and rest under a huge banyan tree. Dhritarashtra, through Sanjaya, laments the death of Duryodhana and asks what the three did next. That night Ashvatthama watches an owl slaughter sleeping crows and decides to copy the tactic by attacking the sleeping enemy camp. This decision drives the rest of the Sauptika Parva.

scenes.B10C001S01: The three survivors flee to a forest at dusk, and Dhritarashtra laments his sons' defeat and asks what the three did next.
scenes.B10C001S02: Ashvatthama cannot sleep, watches an owl kill the sleeping crows in the banyan, and resolves to attack the sleeping enemy by stealth.
scenes.B10C001S03: Ashvatthama tells his companions that Duryodhana is dead and that the Panchalas are celebrating, and asks them for counsel.

shots.B10C001S01H01: Opening invocation to Narayana, Nara and Sarasvati, with the word Jaya.
shots.B10C001S01H02: Sanjaya reports that the three heroes head south, flee east after the Pandava uproar, and rest, tired and thirsty.
shots.B10C001S01H03: Dhritarashtra mourns Duryodhana, his own loss of status and his helplessness, and asks what Kritavarma, Kripa and Drona's son did next.
shots.B10C001S01H04: Sanjaya says the three enter a dense forest full of animals, birds, lakes and flowers, and rest there.
shots.B10C001S01H05: They reach a great banyan tree, perform their evening prayers, and the night falls with noisy creatures.
shots.B10C001S02H01: Kritavarma, Kripa and Ashvatthama sit under the banyan, grieving, and Kripa and Kritavarma fall asleep on the bare ground.
shots.B10C001S02H02: Ashvatthama stays awake and sees an owl attack the sleeping crows in the banyan, killing many of them.
shots.B10C001S02H03: Ashvatthama takes the owl's night attack as a lesson and resolves to strike his sleeping enemies by guile.
shots.B10C001S02H04: He recalls verses that justify attacking an enemy who is tired, asleep, leaderless or unaware.
shots.B10C001S02H05: He settles on a plan to kill the sleeping Pandavas and Panchalas, and wakes Kripa and Kritavarma, who say nothing in reply out of shame.
shots.B10C001S03H01: Ashvatthama, weeping, reports Duryodhana's death, Bhima's kick, and the enemy's celebrations, then asks his companions what to do.

B10C002.summary: Kripa answers Ashvatthama's plan with a long argument that success depends on both destiny and human effort. He says that action is never fruitless, that idleness brings misery, and that Duryodhana ruined himself by ignoring his well-wishers. He advises that the three should first seek counsel from Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Vidura before acting.

scenes.B10C002S01: Kripa argues that success needs both destiny and effort, that action is never wasted, and that Duryodhana brought disaster on himself by ignoring good advice.
scenes.B10C002S02: Kripa proposes that the three go and ask the elders what to do, since advice from wise friends is the sound course.

shots.B10C002S01H01: Kripa says that destiny and exertion together govern all human acts, and neither works alone.
shots.B10C002S01H02: He says effort succeeds through destiny, and the wise combine skill with effort.
shots.B10C002S01H03: He says action is never wasted, idleness brings misery, and enjoying reward without effort invites ridicule.
shots.B10C002S01H04: He says effort fails without destiny, and a man should seek the counsel of the old before acting.
shots.B10C002S01H05: He blames Duryodhana for ignoring his well-wishers and fighting the Pandavas, and says the three are now ruined by following him.
shots.B10C002S02H01: Kripa suggests they ask Dhritarashtra, Gandhari and Vidura what to do, and says those whose efforts fail are under the sway of destiny.

B10C003.summary: Ashvatthama rejects Kripa's advice and argues that every man trusts his own judgment, which shifts with age and fortune. He explains that, though born a Brahmana, he is bound by Kshatriya duty to avenge his father. He then lays out his plan to attack the sleeping Panchalas in their camp and kill them, Dhrishtadyumna included.

scenes.B10C003S01: Ashvatthama says each man trusts his own judgment, explains the division of duties among the castes, and declares he will act as a warrior to avenge his father.
scenes.B10C003S02: Ashvatthama describes how he will attack the Panchalas while they sleep in their camp, after their victory celebration.

shots.B10C003S01H01: Ashvatthama, grieving, answers Kripa by saying each man trusts his own understanding, which changes with time and fortune.
shots.B10C003S01H02: He compares intelligence to a physician's diagnosis and notes that a person's understanding shifts through youth, middle age and decline.
shots.B10C003S01H03: He says a chosen resolve should be carried out with effort, and he now reveals the resolve he has formed.
shots.B10C003S01H04: He recalls how the Creator gave each class its duty: learning to Brahmanas, energy to Kshatriyas, skill to Vaishyas, and service to Shudras.
shots.B10C003S01H05: Born a Brahmana but bound to Kshatriya duty, he says he will avenge his father as a warrior.
shots.B10C003S02H01: He describes his plan to attack the Panchalas while they sleep in camp, slay them including Dhrishtadyumna, and so find peace.

B10C004.summary: Kripa and Kritavarma urge Ashvatthama to rest for the night and promise to fight beside him in the morning. Ashvatthama refuses, citing his grief for his father, his rage at the Pandava victory, and his desire to kill Dhrishtadyumna. He vows to slay his enemies while they sleep before he takes any rest.

scenes.B10C004S01: Kripa and Kritavarma urge rest and promise support in the morning; Ashvatthama refuses, citing his grief and rage, and vows to strike while the enemy sleeps.

shots.B10C004S01H01: Kripa is pleased by Ashvatthama's vengeful resolve, urges him to rest for the night, and promises that he and Kritavarma will fight alongside him in the morning.
shots.B10C004S01H02: Kritavarma joins in: he and Kripa will not retreat without defeating the Pandavas, and they will help him in battle.
shots.B10C004S01H03: Ashvatthama, red-eyed with rage, says grief, anger, greed and lust keep him from sleep, and he cannot rest while his father's killer lives.
shots.B10C004S01H04: He says the Pandavas are protected by Krishna and Arjuna, his rage cannot be calmed, and he will kill the enemy in their sleep before he rests.

B10C005.summary: Kripa again warns Ashvatthama that killing sleeping, disarmed or surrendered men breaks the rules of dharma and would stain his name. Ashvatthama answers that the Pandavas have already broken those rules, listing the unfair deaths of his father, Karna, Bhishma, Bhurishrava and Duryodhana. He yokes his chariot, tells his companions his plan to kill Dhrishtadyumna, and rides with Kripa and Kritavarma to the Panchala camp.

scenes.B10C005S01: Kripa warns against attacking sleeping and unarmed men, and Ashvatthama answers by citing past unfair killings and vows to strike the Panchalas in their sleep.
scenes.B10C005S02: Ashvatthama drives toward the Panchala camp with Kripa and Kritavarma, and they stop at the gate.

shots.B10C005S01H01: Kripa says that a person without understanding or self-control cannot grasp duty, while a wise man learns it by humble attention to elders.
shots.B10C005S01H02: Kripa says well-wishers should hold back a friend who is about to do wrong, and that the one who listens to them prospers.
shots.B10C005S01H03: Kripa argues that killing men who are asleep, unarmed or surrendering is against dharma, and the attack would bring Ashvatthama lasting shame.
shots.B10C005S01H04: Ashvatthama replies that the Pandavas have broken the rules before, citing the unfair deaths of his father, Karna, Bhishma, Bhurishrava and Duryodhana, and vows to kill the Panchalas in their sleep.
shots.B10C005S01H05: Sanjaya reports that Ashvatthama yokes his horses, and when Kritavarma and Kripa ask why, he explains that he will kill Dhrishtadyumna and asks them to arm and wait.
shots.B10C005S02H01: The three ride toward the sleeping Panchala camp, shining like sacrificial fires, and Ashvatthama halts at the gate.

B10C006.summary: At the camp gate Ashvatthama meets a huge, terrifying guardian. Every celestial weapon he hurls is swallowed by the being. Left with no weapons, Ashvatthama recalls Kripa's warning, concludes that fate has turned against him, and resolves to seek the protection of Shiva.

scenes.B10C006S01: Dhritarashtra asks what happened at the gate, and Sanjaya describes the guardian, Ashvatthama's failed attack, and his decision to seek Shiva's protection.

shots.B10C006S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya what Kripa and Kritavarma did when Drona's son stopped at the camp gate.
shots.B10C006S01H02: Sanjaya describes a gigantic, dazzling guardian dressed in tiger and deer skins, with snakes for ornaments, many eyes and a terrifying face.
shots.B10C006S01H03: Ashvatthama hurls a stream of celestial weapons, a blazing dart, a scimitar and a mace, but the being swallows each one.
shots.B10C006S01H04: With his weapons spent, Ashvatthama sees the sky full of images of Krishna, recalls Kripa's counsel, and admits he broke the rules of war by attacking the sleeping and unarmed.
shots.B10C006S01H05: He concludes that fate has turned against him, so his own effort will not succeed, and he resolves to seek the protection of Mahadeva, Shiva.

B10C007.summary: Ashvatthama gets down from his chariot and praises Shiva under many names and titles. A golden altar and a blazing fire appear, surrounded by a host of strange beings. Ashvatthama offers himself into the flames, and Shiva appears, grants him a sword and enters his body, so that he sets out for the enemy camp filled with divine power.

scenes.B10C007S01: Ashvatthama gets down from his chariot and hymns Shiva under many names, then the sacred fire and a host of strange beings appear.
scenes.B10C007S02: Ashvatthama offers himself as a sacrifice, Shiva appears and enters his body, and he sets out for the Panchala camp with the god's followers.

shots.B10C007S01H01: Ashvatthama steps down from his chariot, bows to Shiva, and asks for protection under his many names.
shots.B10C007S01H03: Ashvatthama lists many of Shiva's titles and attributes, from his blue throat to his role as lord of ghostly beings, and asks for protection.
shots.B10C007S01H04: A golden altar and a blazing fire appear, along with many monstrous beings with animal faces and varied bodies.
shots.B10C007S01H05: Those beings carry many weapons, play instruments, dance and roar, and are described as drinkers of blood and fat.
shots.B10C007S02H01: Shiva's followers are described as all-powerful beings who serve the god and are fierce against the enemies of Brahma.
shots.B10C007S02H02: The beings gather around Ashvatthama, wanting to see the slaughter at the hour of sleep, but he feels no fear and offers his own self as a sacrifice.
shots.B10C007S02H03: Ashvatthama addresses the god and climbs onto the altar, offering his soul into the blazing fire.
shots.B10C007S02H04: Shiva appears and says he has been pleased by the devotion of Krishna, and that he protected the Pancalas at Krishna's word, though their lives have run out.
shots.B10C007S02H05: Shiva gives Ashvatthama a sword and enters his body, filling him with divine energy, and invisible beings and Rakshasas follow him toward the enemy camp.

B10C008.summary: Ashvatthama slips into the sleeping Pandava camp at night, kills Dhrishtadyumna in his bed, and then cuts down one warrior after another, including Draupadi's sons, Shikhandi and the Prabhadrakas. Kripa and Kritavarma kill the fugitives at the gate and set the camp on fire, and the night ends in a huge slaughter that leaves the Pandava host destroyed. Dhritarashtra asks why this was not done earlier, and Sanjaya explains that only the absence of Arjuna, Krishna and Satyaki made it possible, since the men were asleep.

scenes.B10C008S01: Ashvatthama enters the camp, kills Dhrishtadyumna in his bed, then kills Uttamauja and Yudhamanyu and the guards who come against him.
scenes.B10C008S02: Ashvatthama moves through the camp with his sword, killing sleeping and unarmed warriors, Draupadi's sons, Shikhandi and many others, while the terrified men fall into confusion.
scenes.B10C008S03: In the chaos, animals break loose, men kill their own comrades, and Kripa and Kritavarma slay the fugitives and set fire to the camp, and Ashvatthama finishes the slaughter.
scenes.B10C008S04: Rakshasas and flesh-eating beings feast on the dead, and at dawn Ashvatthama leaves the camp, meets his companions, and Dhritarashtra asks why he did not act earlier.
scenes.B10C008S05: Sanjaya explains that Ashvatthama had acted only because the Pandava protectors were absent and the men were asleep, and the three rejoice and head to report to the king.

shots.B10C008S01H01: Dhritarashtra asks Sanjaya whether Kripa and Kritavarma fled in fear or fought on, and whether they achieved anything.
shots.B10C008S01H02: Sanjaya says Kripa and Kritavarma wait at the gate, and Ashvatthama urges them to make sure no one escapes, then he enters the camp like Yama.
shots.B10C008S01H03: Ashvatthama slips into the camp through an unguarded spot, finds Dhrishtadyumna asleep on a silk-covered bed, wakes him with a kick, and pins him down.
shots.B10C008S01H04: Dhrishtadyumna begs to be killed with a weapon, but Ashvatthama kicks him to death, and the guards, thinking a demon is attacking, make no outcry.
shots.B10C008S01H05: The women and guards wail, warriors come out, and Ashvatthama kills them with the rudrastra, then kills Uttamauja and Yudhamanyu in their beds.
shots.B10C008S02H01: Ashvatthama moves through the camp killing sleeping and unarmed warriors with his sword, until the terrified men flee or freeze, thinking him a demon.
shots.B10C008S02H02: Draupadi's sons, the Prabhadrakas and Shikhandi come against him, and he kills many of them, including Shikhandi, before attacking the remnants of Virata's army.
shots.B10C008S02H03: He kills the sons, grandsons and followers of Drupada one after another, and the Pandava warriors see the figure of Death-Night they had dreamed of.
shots.B10C008S02H04: Many Pandava archers wake and are cut down, and the rest run about, killing one another in panic, while Ashvatthama is likened to an elephant churning a lake.
shots.B10C008S02H05: The camp is in chaos: men cannot find weapons or recognise one another, animals break their ropes, and the fallen are trampled.
shots.B10C008S03H01: Rakshasas roar with joy as the camp turns into darkness and dust, guards abandon their posts, and men kill comrades they cannot recognise.
shots.B10C008S03H02: Kripa and Kritavarma kill the fugitives at the gate and then set fire to the Pandava camp in three places.
shots.B10C008S03H03: By the light of the fires Ashvatthama cuts down the warriors and leaves the ground strewn with mangled bodies.
shots.B10C008S03H04: The dying call for their kin, and some lament that Arjuna would never kill the sleeping or unarmed, so they blame Rakshasas, and many lie down in despair.
shots.B10C008S03H05: The noise of the dying fades, and before half the night is over Ashvatthama has sent the Pandava host to Yama's abode.
shots.B10C008S04H01: Rakshasas and Pishachas gather, gorging on flesh, drinking blood and dancing in delight.
shots.B10C008S04H02: Other flesh-eating creatures come in huge numbers to feast on the corpses and drink the fat that flows in streams.
shots.B10C008S04H03: At dawn Ashvatthama leaves the camp soaked in blood, his hand fused to his sword, and his grief for his father is said to have eased.
shots.B10C008S04H04: Ashvatthama meets Kripa and Kritavarma, tells them of his feat, and they report killing many Panchalas and Srinjayas at the gates.
shots.B10C008S04H05: Dhritarashtra asks why Ashvatthama, who had fought for Duryodhana, did not achieve this before, and why he did it only after Duryodhana's death.
shots.B10C008S05H01: Sanjaya says fear of the Pandavas and their protectors had held Ashvatthama back, and the feat succeeded only because the men were asleep. The three celebrate the slaughter and set out to tell the king.

B10C009.summary: The three surviving Kaurava warriors find Duryodhana still alive but dying, with his thighs broken and beasts of prey circling him. They lament his fall and blame the Pandavas for an unfair blow, and Ashvatthama tells the king that he has killed Dhrishtadyumna and his sons. Duryodhana, pleased, dies, and Sanjaya reports the death to Dhritarashtra, who is plunged into anxiety.

scenes.B10C009S01: The three find Duryodhana dying on the field, surrounded by beasts of prey, and they lament his fall and blame Bhima and the Pandavas for the unfair blow.
scenes.B10C009S02: Ashvatthama tells the dying king of the night's killings, Duryodhana dies pleased, and Sanjaya reports the news to Dhritarashtra.

shots.B10C009S01H01: Sanjaya describes how the three find Duryodhana still breathing, with broken thighs, bleeding, and surrounded by wolves and hyenas, and they weep over him.
shots.B10C009S01H02: Kripa laments that the mighty king lies on the ground beside his golden mace, and says that Time brings such reversals.
shots.B10C009S01H03: Ashvatthama laments the fall of Duryodhana, blames Bhima for an unfair blow, and blames Yudhishthira for allowing the king's head to be trampled.
shots.B10C009S01H04: Kripa praises Duryodhana's skill with the mace, says a warrior who dies facing the foe reaches heaven, and grieves for Gandhari and Dhritarashtra, while criticising Krishna and Arjuna for standing by.
shots.B10C009S01H05: The three lament that they cannot follow Duryodhana to heaven, and ask how they can live without the king who once protected and enriched them.
shots.B10C009S02H01: Ashvatthama asks the dying king to greet the fallen warriors who have gone before him, and to tell his teacher that Dhrishtadyumna has been slain.
shots.B10C009S02H02: Ashvatthama tells Duryodhana that only seven warriors survive on the Pandava side and only three on his, and reports the slaughter of the Pandava sons and Panchalas.
shots.B10C009S02H03: Duryodhana, revived by the news, says Ashvatthama has done what even Bhishma and Karna could not, and feels as great as Indra, and expects to meet them all in heaven.
shots.B10C009S02H04: Duryodhana falls silent and dies, and the three embrace his body; Sanjaya says he left at dawn and reports that both armies have been destroyed.
shots.B10C009S02H05: Vaishampayana says Dhritarashtra, on hearing of his son's death, sighs deeply and is plunged in anxiety.

B10C010.summary: The charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna brings Yudhishthira the news of the night slaughter. Yudhishthira collapses in grief, reflects that the Pandava victory has turned to defeat through heedlessness, and sends for Draupadi. He then goes to the battlefield and is overwhelmed by the sight of his slain sons and friends.

scenes.B10C010S01: The charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna reports the night massacre, and Yudhishthira collapses and laments that the victory has turned to defeat through heedlessness.
scenes.B10C010S02: Yudhishthira grieves for Draupadi, sends Nakula to fetch her, and goes to the battlefield, where he sees his slain sons and friends and falls senseless.

shots.B10C010S01H01: Vaishampayana says that after the night, the charioteer of Dhrishtadyumna reports the night slaughter to Yudhishthira.
shots.B10C010S01H02: The charioteer says the sons of Draupadi and the children of Drupada were killed in their sleep, and that Kritavarma, Kripa and Ashvatthama destroyed the army; he is the only survivor.
shots.B10C010S01H03: Yudhishthira falls senseless, is held by Satyaki and his brothers, and laments that his victory has turned into defeat and prosperity into misery.
shots.B10C010S01H04: He mourns the warriors who had survived Karna and crossed the great ocean of battle, but were lost through heedlessness.
shots.B10C010S01H05: He says heedlessness is the surest cause of death, and compares the earlier fire of Bhishma's onslaught to the way the Pandava army has now been consumed.
shots.B10C010S02H01: He says heedless men gain neither knowledge nor fame, and blames the Pandavas' heedlessness for letting the enemy survivors kill so many princes.
shots.B10C010S02H02: He grieves for Draupadi, who will be overwhelmed when she learns that her brothers, sons and father have been killed.
shots.B10C010S02H03: He sends Nakula to bring Draupadi, then goes to the battlefield, sees his sons and friends mangled and dead, and collapses in grief.

B10C011.summary: Nakula brings Draupadi to Yudhishthira, and she collapses in grief for her slain sons. Bhima comforts her, and she vows to fast to death unless Ashvatthama is punished and his jewel brought to her. Draupadi urges Bhima to avenge her, and he sets out in pursuit of Ashvatthama's chariot, with Nakula as his charioteer.

scenes.B10C011S01: Yudhishthira is overwhelmed by grief, Nakula brings Draupadi, who collapses, and she vows to fast to death unless Ashvatthama is punished and his jewel is brought to her.
scenes.B10C011S02: Draupadi asks Bhima to avenge her by slaying Ashvatthama, and Bhima sets out from the camp in pursuit of Ashvatthama's chariot.

shots.B10C011S01H01: Vaishampayana says Yudhishthira is overwhelmed by the slaughter of his sons, grandsons, brothers and allies, and his friends try to comfort him.
shots.B10C011S01H02: Nakula arrives with Draupadi, who has learned of the killing of her sons at Upaplavya, and she falls down in grief before Yudhishthira.
shots.B10C011S01H03: Bhima lifts her up and holds her, and Draupadi speaks bitterly, then vows to fast to death unless Drona's son is punished.
shots.B10C011S01H04: Yudhishthira tells her that her sons died nobly, and asks how she can be sure that Ashvatthama has fallen, since he has gone into a forest.
shots.B10C011S01H05: Draupadi says she has heard Ashvatthama wears a jewel on his head, and she will live only if she sees it brought to her and places it on Yudhishthira's head.
shots.B10C011S02H01: Draupadi asks Bhima to avenge her, recalling his past rescues at Varanavata, from Hidimba, and at Virata's city, and urges him to slay Drona's son.
shots.B10C011S02H02: Bhima takes up his bow, Nakula drives his chariot, and he sets out from the Pandava camp in pursuit of Ashvatthama's chariot.

B10C012.summary: Krishna warns Yudhishthira that Ashvatthama, who holds the brahmashira weapon, is a danger to Bhima. He recounts how Ashvatthama once came to Dvaraka asking for Krishna's discus in exchange for the brahmashira, and how the discus could not be lifted and was refused. Krishna notes that no close relative ever asked for such a thing, so Ashvatthama's request shows a wrathful and dangerous mind.

scenes.B10C012S01: Krishna warns Yudhishthira that Bhima is in danger, explains that Drona taught Ashvatthama the brahmashira reluctantly, and recalls Ashvatthama's first request for the discus at Dvaraka.
scenes.B10C012S02: Krishna reports the rest of the meeting: relatives never asked such a thing, Ashvatthama admits he meant to fight Krishna with the discus, and he then leaves Dvaraka, and Bhima must be protected from him.

shots.B10C012S01H01: Vaishampayana says Krishna urges Yudhishthira to help Bhima, who is grieving and alone, and warns that Ashvatthama holds the brahmashira, a weapon Drona taught him only with reluctance and an order never to use it against humans.
shots.B10C012S01H02: Krishna recalls that Ashvatthama came to him on the sea coast at Dvaraka and offered the brahmashira in exchange for the discus.
shots.B10C012S01H03: Krishna says he offered Ashvatthama his bow, dart, discus and mace instead, and told him to take whichever he could wield.
shots.B10C012S01H04: Ashvatthama tries to lift the discus with his left hand and then his right, fails to move it, and gives up exhausted.
shots.B10C012S01H05: Krishna rebukes him, saying that Arjuna, his closest friend, would never have asked such a thing, and that it is an unworthy request for a Brahmana.
shots.B10C012S02H01: Krishna says his son Pradyumna, born after long austerities, never asked for the discus either.
shots.B10C012S02H02: Krishna says Rama, Gada, Samba and the other Vrishni and Andhaka warriors never asked for it, and asks Ashvatthama whom he would fight with it.
shots.B10C012S02H03: Ashvatthama says he meant to fight Krishna with the discus, and that now that he has failed, he is leaving.
shots.B10C012S02H04: Ashvatthama leaves Dvaraka with horses, wealth and gems, and Krishna warns that he is wrathful and knows the brahmashira, so Bhima must be guarded.

B10C013.summary: Krishna mounts his chariot with Arjuna and Yudhishthira and drives after Bhima, who is charging toward Ashvatthama. They catch up with Bhima at the bank of the Ganga, where Vyasa and other sages are seated, and Ashvatthama is there in grass garments. Ashvatthama turns a blade of grass into the brahmashira and releases it against the Pandavas, and it blazes like the fire that ends the world.

scenes.B10C013S01: Krishna's chariot is described, and Krishna drives Arjuna and Yudhishthira after Bhima, and Ashvatthama prepares the brahmashira against the Pandavas.

shots.B10C013S01H01: Vaishampayana describes Krishna mounting his chariot, with its horses, standard and Garuda emblem.
shots.B10C013S01H02: Arjuna and Yudhishthira ride with Krishna, and the swift horses carry them off in pursuit.
shots.B10C013S01H03: They catch up with Bhima, who ignores them and charges on, and at the bank of the Ganga they see Vyasa and sages, and Ashvatthama in grass garments. Bhima calls out for him to wait.
shots.B10C013S01H04: Ashvatthama, seeing the Pandavas coming, turns a blade of grass into the brahmashira, says it is for the destruction of the Pandavas, and releases it, and a fire blazes out that threatens all three worlds.

B10C014.summary: Krishna sees Ashvatthama's intent and tells Arjuna to use the weapon that can neutralise all others. Arjuna releases his own brahmashira to counter it, and the two weapons blaze, bringing thunder, meteors and trembling to the world. Narada and Vyasa step between the weapons to calm the heroes and ask why they used such weapons against men.

scenes.B10C014S01: Krishna urges Arjuna to counter the weapon, Arjuna releases his own brahmashira, and the sages Narada and Vyasa step between the two blazing weapons.

shots.B10C014S01H01: Vaishampayana says Krishna reads Ashvatthama's intent and tells Arjuna to use the counter-weapon that Drona taught him to protect them all.
shots.B10C014S01H02: Arjuna dismounts, bows to the gods and his elders, wishes well to all, and releases his weapon to neutralise Ashvatthama's.
shots.B10C014S01H03: The two weapons blaze, thunder and meteors fall, and the earth trembles, until Narada and Vyasa come and stand between the two weapons to pacify the heroes.
shots.B10C014S01H04: The two sages ask why the heroes have used such weapons on men, since the fallen warriors, skilled as they were, never did so.

B10C015.summary: Arjuna withdraws his weapon at the sages' urging, which only a celibate, truthful and obedient warrior can do. Ashvatthama admits he released his weapon out of fear of Bhima and cannot recall it. Vyasa persuades him to yield his gem, but Ashvatthama finally agrees to aim the weapon at the wombs of the Pandava women.

scenes.B10C015S01: Arjuna asks the sages for help and withdraws his weapon, Vyasa explains why it matters, and Ashvatthama admits he cannot recall his own weapon and offers his gem.
scenes.B10C015S02: Vyasa tells Ashvatthama to turn the weapon away from the Pandavas, and he directs it at the wombs of the Pandava women.

shots.B10C015S01H01: Arjuna sees the two sages blazing like fire, folds his hands, and asks them to find a way to save the Pandavas and the three worlds, since his weapon would otherwise destroy them.
shots.B10C015S01H02: Arjuna withdraws his weapon. The narrator explains that only a celibate, truthful and obedient warrior like Arjuna could do so.
shots.B10C015S01H03: Ashvatthama tells the sage that he released the weapon out of fear of Bhima, that he cannot withdraw it, and that it will destroy the Pandavas.
shots.B10C015S01H04: Vyasa says Arjuna used his weapon only to counter it, asks Ashvatthama to recall his weapon and give up his gem, and promises the Pandavas will spare his life in return.
shots.B10C015S01H05: Ashvatthama says the gem is precious and he is loath to part with it, but he offers it, and says he cannot recall the weapon, so he will send it against the Pandava women's wombs.
shots.B10C015S02H01: Vyasa tells Ashvatthama to do this, but to pursue no other purpose.
shots.B10C015S02H02: Ashvatthama throws the weapon into the wombs of the Pandava women.

B10C016.summary: Krishna declares that Virata's daughter will bear a child, Parikshit, who will survive the weapon and rule the kingdom. Ashvatthama defies him, but Krishna curses him to wander for three thousand years, and Vyasa confirms the curse. Ashvatthama gives up his gem, the Pandavas bring it to Draupadi, and she gives it to Yudhishthira, ending her fast.

scenes.B10C016S01: Krishna foretells that Parikshit will be born and survive, Ashvatthama defies him, Krishna curses him to wander, and Vyasa and Ashvatthama accept the sentence.
scenes.B10C016S02: Ashvatthama hands over his gem and goes into the forest, and the Pandavas take the gem back to Draupadi, where Bhima recalls her bitter words to Krishna.
scenes.B10C016S03: Draupadi returns the gem to Yudhishthira, who places it on his head, and she gives up her vow.

shots.B10C016S01H01: Vaishampayana says that Krishna, seeing the weapon thrown, predicts that a child named Parikshit will be born to Virata's daughter, and Ashvatthama replies that Krishna's words will not come true.
shots.B10C016S01H02: Krishna answers that the child will die but be revived, calls Ashvatthama a coward and a killer of children, and curses him to wander alone for three thousand years.
shots.B10C016S01H03: Krishna says Parikshit will grow up, learn the Vedas and weapons, and rule the Kuru kingdom, and that he will revive the child himself.
shots.B10C016S01H04: Vyasa says that since Ashvatthama acted cruelly against the Pandavas, Krishna's words will come true in his case.
shots.B10C016S01H05: Ashvatthama accepts the sentence, saying he will live among men with the sage's words.
shots.B10C016S02H01: Ashvatthama says he accepts Krishna's and Vyasa's words, which he asks to come true.
shots.B10C016S02H02: Ashvatthama hands the gem to the Pandavas and leaves reluctantly for the forest, and the Pandavas take the gem to Draupadi, who is fasting, with Krishna, Vyasa and Narada.
shots.B10C016S02H03: The Pandavas return to camp, find Draupadi in grief, and sit around her.
shots.B10C016S02H04: Bhima gives her the gem and says her sons' slayer has been beaten, then reminds her of her bitter words to Krishna during the peace mission.
shots.B10C016S02H05: Bhima boasts that Duryodhana and Duhshasana have been slain, the debt is paid, and Ashvatthama has been stripped of his gem and weapons.
shots.B10C016S03H01: Draupadi says she only wanted repayment for the injury, respects Ashvatthama as a teacher's son, and asks Yudhishthira to wear the gem. He places it on his head, and she gives up her vow. Yudhishthira then asks Krishna a question.

B10C017.summary: Yudhishthira asks Krishna how Ashvatthama, a warrior of little skill, could kill so many great fighters single-handed. The answer is that Ashvatthama had won the favour of Mahadeva, and the story of Rudra's withdrawal from the work of creation is told to explain the god's power. Rudra, angered that the creatures had multiplied without him, retreats to the mountains to practise harsher austerities.

scenes.B10C017S01: Yudhishthira asks how Ashvatthama could do such damage, and the answer tells how Brahma made beings and how Rudra withdrew to the water and then to the mountains in anger.

shots.B10C017S01H01: Vaishampayana says Yudhishthira, grieving, asks Krishna how Ashvatthama could kill his sons, Drupada's children and Dhrishtadyumna single-handed.
shots.B10C017S01H02: The answer is that Ashvatthama had sought the aid of Mahadeva, who can grant great strength, and that Shiva is the beginning, middle and end of all creatures.
shots.B10C017S01H03: Brahma asks Rudra to create beings, and Rudra goes into the water to practise austerities, so Brahma creates another being to do the work.
shots.B10C017S01H04: The new beings turn on Brahma, wanting to devour him, so he assigns plants and weaker creatures as their food, and they multiply.
shots.B10C017S01H05: Rudra returns, sees the creatures multiplying without him, and in anger withdraws his generative organ into the earth, then goes to the Menjavat mountains to practise harsher austerities.

B10C018.summary: The gods hold a sacrifice without giving Rudra a share, and Rudra, in anger, builds a bow and attacks it, injuring the gods and breaking the sacrifice. When the gods beg for mercy, Rudra restores their limbs and the sacrifice and is given offerings as his share. The narrative concludes that Ashvatthama's feats were done through Shiva's grace, so Yudhishthira should not dwell on them but act next.

scenes.B10C018S01: The gods leave Rudra out of their sacrifice, Rudra attacks it, and after they beg for mercy he restores them, and the answer ends by telling Yudhishthira that Ashvatthama's deeds came from Shiva's grace.
scenes.B10C018S02: The closing colophon marks the end of the Sauptika Parva and credits the Mahabharata to Vyasa.

shots.B10C018S01H01: After the Krita age, the gods prepare a sacrifice and decide among themselves who will receive the offerings.
shots.B10C018S01H02: They leave out Rudra, who takes a bow made from parts of the sacrifice and sets out to destroy it.
shots.B10C018S01H03: Rudra arrives as a brahmacari with the bow, terrifying the earth, the wind and the gods, and wounds the sacrifice, which flees as a deer while he pursues it.
shots.B10C018S01H04: Rudra breaks the arms of Savitri, plucks the eyes of Bhaga and the teeth of Pushan, and paralyses the gods. Their plea for mercy makes the string of his bow break.
shots.B10C018S01H05: Rudra restores the limbs and the sacrifice, and the gods give him shares of the offerings. The answer concludes that Ashvatthama's deeds were done through Shiva's grace, and that Yudhishthira should now act.
shots.B10C018S02H01: Closing line: the Sauptika Parva ends.
